domain.name: secretary
domain.one_line: Classical no-information secretary problem: select the overall-best candidate from 100 uniformly randomly ordered arrivals using relative ranks only.

n_candidates.domain: integer >= 2, known before the first arrival
n_candidates.source: classical finite secretary problem; this study fixes N=100

arrival_order.domain: episode state initialized at reset as a uniformly random permutation of absolute ranks 1..N, with rank 1 best; hidden thereafter
arrival_order.source: classical random-order assumption; corrected after review so the realization belongs to episode state, not scenario configuration

relative_rank.domain: integer 1..t at the t-th arrival (one-based); 1 means best among candidates seen so far
relative_rank.source: the no-information observation structure confirmed in Phase A

accept.domain: binary {0,1}; reject or irrevocably accept the current candidate, with either action legal even for a non-record
accept.source: the stopping decision confirmed in Phase A

selected_rank.domain: the selected candidate's hidden absolute rank; the last candidate is selected if every earlier candidate was rejected
selected_rank.source: exactly-one-selection and forced-final-candidate rules confirmed in Phase A

out_of_scope: full-information secretary variants that reveal absolute candidate quality before selection
recall, multiple selections, hiring costs, and rejection costs
objectives based primarily on expected rank rather than probability of selecting the single best candidate
dynamics: episode start: nature draws a uniformly random permutation of ranks 1..N and keeps it hidden
at arrival t the decision-maker observes t and the candidate's rank relative to the first t candidates
the decision-maker chooses reject or accept; acceptance ends the episode and cannot be recalled
if all first N-1 candidates are rejected, candidate N is selected regardless of the final reject action
the terminal payoff is one exactly when the selected candidate has absolute rank 1, otherwise zero

notation.period: zero-based arrival index t; the human-facing arrival number is t+1
notation.relative_rank: R_t, rank among arrivals 0..t with 1 best
notation.selected_rank: absolute rank of the selected candidate, with 1 globally best

constants.name: n_candidates
constants.desc: N, the known number of candidates; fixed at 100 for this specialist campaign

constants.name: initial_arrival_order
constants.desc: interpreter initialization draw copied into the latent arrival_order state at reset; not a scenario field in generated domain code

samplers.name: standard
samplers.desc: fresh uniformly random permutation of ranks 1..N for every episode

state_variables.name: period
state_variables.desc: zero-based index of the candidate currently presented; increments after the decision

state_variables.name: relative_rank
state_variables.desc: current candidate's one-based rank among candidates seen so far; 1 means a record, and 0 is the terminal sentinel

state_variables.name: selected
state_variables.desc: 1 after a candidate is selected; selection immediately terminates the episode

state_variables.name: arrival_order
state_variables.desc: the hidden absolute-rank permutation realized during episode initialization and retained as episode state

info_fields.name: decision_relative_rank
info_fields.desc: relative rank visible when the action was chosen; retained for trajectory checking

info_fields.name: candidate_rank
info_fields.desc: hidden absolute rank of the current candidate; diagnostic only and never observed before acting

info_fields.name: selected_rank
info_fields.desc: hidden absolute rank if selection occurred this period, otherwise 0

decisions.name: accept

type.rationale: the user confirmed the binary irrevocable accept/reject decision

bounds.rationale: 0=reject and 1=accept; the user confirmed both actions remain legal for every candidate

decisions.desc: 0 rejects the current candidate; 1 irrevocably selects that candidate

updates: selected_rank = candidate_rank if accept == 1 or period == T - 1 else 0
relative_rank = (1 + sum(1 for j in range(period) if arrival_order[j] < arrival_order[period])) if period < T and selected == 0 else 0

invariants.name: reported_relative_rank_is_correct
invariants.expr: decision_relative_rank == 1 + sum(1 for j in range(t) if arrival_order[j] < arrival_order[t])
invariants.desc: the rank shown to the decision-maker is exactly the current candidate's rank among everyone seen so far

invariants.name: selection_rule
invariants.desc: a candidate is selected exactly when accept is chosen or the final candidate forces selection

invariants.name: selected_rank_matches_candidate
invariants.expr: selected_rank == candidate_rank if selected == 1 else selected_rank == 0
invariants.desc: selection records exactly the presented candidate's hidden absolute rank and records no rank on rejection

invariants.name: success_means_global_best
invariants.desc: success occurs exactly when the selected candidate is the unique overall best

action_modes.name: accept
action_modes.desc: binary identity encoding: 0 rejects and 1 accepts; the final reject is resolved by the MDP's forced-selection rule

reward_modes.name: success
reward_modes.desc: zero until selection, then one iff the selected candidate is globally best

requires_memory.rationale: the hidden permutation triggers the conservative memory heuristic, but the user confirmed that current position and current relative rank form the sufficient decision state for the classical secretary problem

obs_normalization.rationale: time-to-go ranges to 100 while relative rank has a position-dependent scale; normalization keeps the two inputs numerically comparable

eval_metrics.name: expected_selected_rank
eval_metrics.desc: absolute rank of the selected candidate, averaged across evaluation episodes; lower is better but it never selects or gates a model
eval_metrics.source: objective candidate 'expected selected rank', declined at Phase A and retained as report-only

benchmarks.name: dp
benchmarks.basis: finite-horizon backward induction on (position, relative rank); exact for the N=100 classical secretary MDP

benchmarks.name: threshold
benchmarks.basis: Gilbert-Mosteller finite-N optimal rule: reject the first r candidates, then accept the next record, with r maximizing the exact success probability; forced final selection

benchmarks.name: random
benchmarks.basis: independent fair reject/accept action at every decision, with forced final selection

benchmarks.name: fitted
benchmarks.basis: skip-then-accept-record rule fitted from the winning PPO action surface and scored independently under the shared protocol

tier2.claim: the learned policy rejects an initial prefix and then accepts the next record, agreeing with the exact finite-N threshold rule
tier2.instrument: policy probe over every (position, relative-rank) observation, fitted cutoff, paired score against the exact threshold benchmark

assumptions_log: N=100 is the human-confirmed specialist design point; no horizon grid is trained.
Absolute ranks are 1..100 with 1 best; reset initializes a fresh uniform permutation into hidden episode state, while the scenario contains only setting hyperparameters.
The policy observes only time-to-go and the current candidate's relative rank; absolute ranks and future arrivals remain hidden.
Accept/reject is an unmasked discrete action; accepting a non-record is legal and loses.
Rejecting the final candidate still selects that candidate, ensuring exactly one selection.
The objective is undiscounted probability of selecting the overall best; expected selected rank is report-only.
No recurrent memory is used because (position, relative rank) is sufficient for the classical optimal stopping decision.
No categorical scenario modes are present, so cross-mode leaderboard stance is not applicable.
